datasets.name: banks
datasets.title: Credit institutions and IBAN bank codes
datasets.description: The credit institutions in the register of the National Bank of Romania: banks, housing banks, mortgage banks, credit cooperatives and their central bank, branches of foreign credit institutions, and those removed from the register, with the day of removal. codes.jsonl gives the bank code of a Romanian IBAN, the four letters after the check digits, with the BIC: the Romanian BICs of the SWIFT BIC-to-LEI mapping table, joined to the register by LEI. A branch the register gives no LEI for is joined by the LEI of its head office, stated in head_office_lei. Credit cooperatives have no code of their own: their accounts carry the code of their central bank. TREZ, the State Treasury, is added from Order MFP 1650/2014. A code can name an institution that was removed: the BIC of an absorbed bank may stay with the bank that absorbed it. Names and addresses are as BNR writes them; BNR shows some Romanian letters as a question mark.

source.name: National Bank of Romania, register of credit institutions (https://www.bnr.ro/2349-registre-si-liste); SWIFT BIC-to-LEI mapping table of 2026-10-30, published by GLEIF (https://www.gleif.org/en/lei-data/lei-mapping/download-bic-to-lei-relationship-files)
source.licence: Register: facts taken from the public register BNR keeps under Regulation 1/2007; BNR's own terms for its content: https://www.bnr.ro/2281-termeni-si-conditii. BICs: royalty-free licence of SWIFT for any use, with this notice: SWIFT © and database rights October 2026. All rights reserved. This Mapping Table has been developed by SWIFT. Any use of the Mapping Table, in whole or in part, is subject to the BIC/LEI Mapping Table License Agreement as published with the Mapping Table available on GLEIF's website. The Mapping Table is updated monthly. For the latest BIC information and updates, always refer to www.swift.com/bic .

datasets.name: bnr-currencies

datasets.description: The currencies for which the National Bank of Romania (BNR) publishes a reference rate against the leu, with the number of units the rate is given for and the first and last day of publication, from 2005. datasets.name: caen
datasets.title: Classification of economic activities in Romania (CAEN), Rev.2 and Rev.3, with the links between them
datasets.description: The sections, divisions, groups and classes of CAEN Rev.2 and CAEN Rev.3, with their names in Romanian, as the National Trade Register Office (ONRC) uses them to decode the activities of companies. A code is unique only within its version and level: Rev.2 and Rev.3 use some of the same codes for other activities, so always read the version with the code. Rev.3 corresponds to NACE Rev.2.1 and Rev.2 to NACE Rev.2. The older versions of the source (1998 and 2003) are not here. The days from which each version applies are not in the source. correspondence.jsonl links each class of Rev.2 to the classes of Rev.3 that take its activities, from the correspondence table of Eurostat between NACE Rev.2 and NACE Rev.2.1: CAEN writes the NACE class codes without the dot. Every class of Rev.2 has a link. Classes of Rev.3 with no class of Rev.2 behind them: 4689.

source.name: National Trade Register Office (ONRC), N_CAEN.CSV and N_VERSIUNE_CAEN.CSV of its newest nomenclatures on data.gov.ro; links from Eurostat, correspondence table NACE Rev.2.1 to NACE Rev.2 (http://data.europa.eu/ux2/nace2.1/NACE2.1_NACE2), published by the Publications Office of the European Union
source.licence: CC BY 4.0, under which ONRC publishes the nomenclatures on data.gov.ro; the correspondence table under the European Commission reuse notice (Decision 2011/833/EU): reuse allowed with the source acknowledged

datasets.name: chart-of-accounts
datasets.title: General chart of accounts (OMFP 1802/2014)
datasets.description: The general chart of accounts for double-entry bookkeeping of companies, chapter 14 of the accounting regulations approved by OMFP 1802/2014: classes, groups, accounts and subaccounts, with the function the order gives (A for asset, P for liability, A/P for both) where it gives one; a subaccount without one takes the function of its account. role marks what the closing of the result needs: the accounts of class 6 are expenses, those of class 7 income, and 121 is the result. notes are the notes of the order on the account. The chart is the one in force on 2026-01-01, the first day the dataset covers; an account with valid_from null was in force that day. A later change of the chart gives the day it applies from and the act that made it. Names are as the order writes them.

datasets.name: countries
datasets.title: Countries and territories
datasets.description: Countries and territories with their ISO 3166-1 codes, their names in Romanian and English, whether they are a member state of the European Union today, whether they are in the European Union for VAT, with their VAT prefix, and the code with which an electronic invoice under EN 16931, as e-Factura, names them. Northern Ireland is not a country, but invoices name it XI and VIES answers for the prefix XI, so it is here as an entry only for invoices, with no alpha-3 code. Withdrawn entries stay, with their last day of use, so an alpha-2 code can appear on a withdrawn entry and on a current one; the alpha-3 code is unique where there is one. Kosovo is not in ISO 3166-1 and is listed with the user-assigned codes XK and XKX. Names are the short names the European Union institutions use, with Romanian letters written with the comma below and without the asterisk the source puts on Kosovo. A name does not state a position on the status of a territory.

source.name: Publications Office of the European Union, Countries and territories authority table; VAT prefixes from the VIES service of the European Commission (https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/rest-api/check-status); invoice codes from the country list of the EN 16931 code lists of the European Commission

datasets.name: efactura
datasets.title: Codes accepted by e-Factura
datasets.description: The codes the e-Factura system of ANAF accepts in an invoice, as its validation package 1.0.9 checks them: for each check of a code list (BR-CL-*) and each check of CIUS-RO that narrows one (BR-RO-*), every code it accepts. The package carries its own copy of the European lists, which can be older than en16931-codes: a code new in en16931-codes can be refused by ANAF, and a code that left en16931-codes can still be accepted. Names are not here: read them from the file the list field names. Also the subdivision codes CIUS-RO asks for in a Romanian address: RO-AB to RO-VS for the county, and SECTOR1 to SECTOR6 as the city in Bucharest. Only facts are taken from the package; its rules decide, and they are not here.

source.name: Ministry of Finance, e-Factura validation package ro16931-ubl-1.0.9 (https://mfinante.gov.ro/static/10/eFactura/ro16931-ubl-1.0.9.zip), files codelist/EN16931-UBL-codes.sch and cius-ro/RO16931-rules.sch
source.licence: Facts taken from the package: which codes each check accepts. The package states no licence and no text of it is copied

datasets.name: en16931-codes
datasets.title: Code lists of the European standard on e-invoicing, EN 16931
datasets.description: The code lists an invoice under EN 16931 uses, as the European Commission publishes them for the standard: units of measure, currencies, VAT categories and exemption reasons, payment means, document types, electronic address and identifier schemes, allowance and charge reasons, item schemes, reference and text qualifiers, attachment types. They are European, not Romanian; the e-Factura dataset says which codes ANAF accepts. Every archive the Commission still publishes is read, from the one used from 2021-05-17 to the one used from 2026-11-15, so a code that left a list stays with its last day. A code can come back later, as a new row. Names are in English as in the lists. The currencies with a BNR rate are in bnr-currencies, by the same code. The country list of the archives is not here: the countries are in the countries dataset. An invoice writes Kosovo 1A, where countries has XK, and may write XI for Northern Ireland, which countries leaves out.

source.name: European Commission, Registry of supporting artefacts to implement EN16931, genericode archives used from 2021-05-17 to 2026-11-15
source.licence: European Commission reuse notice (Decision 2011/833/EU, CC BY 4.0 for EU content): reuse allowed with the source acknowledged. The codes and their names come from UN/CEFACT, ISO, IANA and the Commission; each file names its origin

datasets.name: mfp-localities
datasets.title: Localities of the Ministry of Finance with their SIRUTA code
datasets.description: The localities of the nomenclature of the Ministry of Finance (MFP), whose codes ANAF uses in addresses, with the SIRUTA code each matches. MFP gives a SIRUTA code of its own, kept in mfp_siruta, which is wrong for many administrative units (1008 for Alba Iulia, which SIRUTA does not have). siruta is that code when SIRUTA has it in the same county under the same name (match code); otherwise the one place of the county with the name, an administrative unit for a municipality, town, commune or sector and a locality for the others (match name); otherwise null. Of 17317 localities, 16793 match by code, 378 by name, and 146 not: places SIRUTA no longer has, names written another way, the entries for people without a home in Romania, and a few test rows. uat is the administrative unit or Bucharest sector of siruta. Names are as MFP writes them.

source.name: Ministry of Finance, nomenclatures of counties, locality types and localities (https://www.mfinante.gov.ro/static/40/Mfp/nomenclatoare/)
source.licence: Facts taken from the nomenclatures: the codes, names, types and postal codes of the localities. MFP states no licence for them

datasets.name: public-holidays
datasets.title: Public holidays of Romania
datasets.description: The days on which no work is done by law, as rules that give the days of any year: a fixed month and day, or a number of days from Orthodox Easter Sunday. Orthodox Easter Sunday is the Julian computus moved to the civil calendar. A day can come from two rules, such as the second day of Pentecost on 1 June. Days declared free by a Government decision for one year only are not included. The two days each of three yearly feasts of other legal religions have no fixed date and are not included.

source.name: Labour Code (Law 53/2003, republished), article 139 (1); Orthodox Easter is computed

datasets.name: reges
datasets.title: Nomenclatures of REGES-Online
datasets.description: The nomenclatures of REGES-Online, the employee register of the Labour Inspectorate, as its public nomenclature service gives them: COR occupations in every version with the current one marked, activity domains (CAEN), counties and localities with their SIRUTA codes, nationalities, legal and organisation forms, contract types, working time, grounds for termination, suspension and secondment, predefined bonuses, identity documents, disability grades, education levels, and the lists of the public pay law 153/2017. One file for each list, named after it; entries as REGES gives them, with their REGES identifier, which a message to REGES needs. Names are written as REGES writes them, some with Romanian letters and some without. The localities inside each county are left out of judet.jsonl: localitate.jsonl has them, with judetId. Lists that have no entry today are not here: tipSporAngajator.

datasets.name: single-entry-categories
datasets.title: Income and expense categories of single-entry bookkeeping
datasets.description: The categories of income and expense of independent activities whose net income is set in the real system, on the basis of single-entry bookkeeping: the letters of article 68 of the Fiscal Code (Law 227/2015) on gross income (income), what is not gross income (not-income), the conditions and kinds of deductible expenses (deductible), the expenses deductible within limits (limited) and the non-deductible expenses (non-deductible). OMFP 170/2015 sets the registers of single entry, not a chart: these categories are what the law gives to sort its entries. text is the letter as the code writes it; notes are the notes of the portal on how a change applies, for instance to the income of a whole year. The categories are those in force on 2026-01-01, the first day the dataset covers; a later change gives the day it took effect and the act, as the portal notes them.

source.name: Legislative Portal, consolidated forms of the Fiscal Code (Law 227/2015) from 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-18, article 68 (https://legislatie.just.ro/Public/DetaliiDocument/171282)

datasets.name: siruta
datasets.title: Administrative-territorial units of Romania (SIRUTA)
datasets.description: The register of administrative-territorial units of Romania kept by the National Institute of Statistics (INS), edition S1 2026: counties and Bucharest, municipalities, towns and communes, and the localities and Bucharest sectors in them, with their SIRUTA codes. Names are in capitals as INS writes them. INS writes them without Romanian letters; the letters come from the copy INS publishes on data.gov.ro, used only where its letters are the INS letters with the marks, and written with the comma below. 4 names keep the INS spelling without the marks, because the two copies spell them differently. The register has no history and no code has left it since 2013. A code is never removed here: if INS drops one, the dataset is not rebuilt until a person decides how it ends. The check digit of the INS methodology does not hold for some codes, so do not reject a code by it.

source.name: National Institute of Statistics (INS), SIRUTA register, edition S1 2026 (https://insse.ro/cms/files/siruta/2026/SIRUTA_S1_2026.rar); names with Romanian letters from the SIRUTA files INS publishes on data.gov.ro
source.licence: CC BY 4.0, under which INS publishes SIRUTA on data.gov.ro (https://data.gov.ro/organization/institutul-national-de-statistica)

datasets.update: INS publishes a new edition twice a year, for the first half and for the whole year

datasets.name: tax-offices
datasets.title: ANAF fiscal units and the localities they serve
datasets.description: The regional directorates of public finance, the county administrations and the fiscal units of ANAF, with their contact, and for each locality of SIRUTA that ANAF names the unit that serves it, under the territorial competence set by Order ANAF 3631/2015. A locality is mostly an administrative unit; ANAF names some villages and the sectors of Bucharest, and uat gives the administrative unit each is in. To find the unit of an address, look up its village first, then its administrative unit. Large taxpayers are served by the Directorate General for Large Taxpayers (DGAMC), which the page does not list; medium taxpayers and non-residents have units of their own, which serve no locality here. Names and contacts are as ANAF writes them.

source.name: ANAF, territorial competence of the fiscal units (https://static.anaf.ro/static/10/Anaf/AsistentaContribuabili_r/telefoane_judete/Regiuni.htm)

datasets.name: treasury
datasets.title: State Treasury units and the IBAN of their accounts
datasets.description: The operative units of the State Treasury, each with its code, county and SIRUTA code, and the accounts taxes and other payments go to, as ANAF lists them for each unit. The IBAN of an account at a unit is RO, two check digits (ISO 13616, mod 97), TREZ, the three digits of the unit and iban_suffix: an account has the same suffix and name at every unit, so it is listed once, with the units that have it. published is the earliest publication date ANAF gives for the account at any unit. The accounts of the last sections of a list have no funding source. Names are as ANAF writes them, without Romanian letters. A unit's SIRUTA code is matched by name; Ilfov and Gura Lotrului name no administrative unit and have none.

source.name: ANAF, IBAN codes of the State Treasury units (https://www.anaf.ro/anaf/internet/ANAF/asistenta_contribuabili/plata_oblig_fiscale/coduri_iban)
source.licence: Facts taken from the lists: the units, which accounts each has and their IBAN. ANAF states no licence for them. The account names are those of the budget classification, set by order of the Minister of Finance, which is not subject to copyright (Law 8/1996, article 9)

datasets.name: vat-numbers

datasets.description: How a VAT number looks in each European jurisdiction: the prefix, the format in words and as a regular expression, and the name of the tax in the local language. It says which jurisdictions are in the European Union for VAT. A number that fits the pattern is well formed; whether it is registered is a question for VIES or the national register.
